title: What happened in AI — Nov 4, 2026
intro: Heavier agent scaffolding lost to simpler setups: a 100-task benchmark found Claude Code with more thinking beat a 37-skill, 17-agent harness that cost 8× more.

NVIDIA's result that 16K contexts with compaction hold accuracy points the same way: cut context and orchestration, not capability. Kimi K3.1 Pro's day-0 vLLM support shows open-weight serving catching up fast.
highlights: Extended thinking beat a 37-skill, 17-agent harness that cost 8× more.
NVIDIA: frontier agents lose little accuracy at 16K context with compaction; long context costs up to 7× more per token.
Cleric's ~40-agent rewrite made evals 5× faster and 100× cheaper.
Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T MoE, open weights) had day-0 vLLM support.
Glow Labs: coding agents are installing deprecated MCP servers with known flaws.
H200 loses money fully busy; B300 profits at 35% utilization.

categories.name: Agent harnesses: less scaffolding, durable memory
